To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The Estonian power system has the potential of utilizing loads for power ancillary services.
demand side management in small power systems is a feasible and beneficial solution for both, power system operator and the consumer.
the Estonian power system is a small system with a high share of renewable energy sources and the potential to increase the flexibility of the system through demand side management is limited.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: • How can demand side management be used in a small power system?
the following questions: What are the main challenges for the development and implementation of demand side management in small power systems?

the following: - The analysis of the Estonian electricity sector, the main players and the current situation in terms of demand side management and ancillary services - The analysis of potential for demand side management in three main energy intensive sectors in Estonia: industry, district heating and transport - The analysis of demand side response and ancillary services in other European small power systems - The development of business case for the customers and the system operator - The development of demand side management business case for Estonian small power system
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Estonian energy sector is still in a transition period.
the potential is there, but the implementation is still missing.
the Estonian energy intensive economic sectors are not yet sufficiently flexible to be utilized for ancillary services in the Estonian power system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
demand side management can be used for providing additional reserves for the power system.

demand side flexibility can provide incentives not only for system operator but also the customers who are able to optimize their processes to gain higher energy efficiency and at same time provide flexibility to the power system.
we have developed a methodology for the Estonian case study for the demand side management and the demand side response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
demand side response is a valuable resource for the power system.
demand-side flexibility is a viable and economically beneficial alternative to traditional ancillary reserves in a small power system.

there is a potential for demand side flexibility in the Estonian power system, but it needs further development and incentives to make it more attractive for both, the customer as well as the power system operator.
